findings.label: Frontal bossing and maxillary hyperplasia
findings.evidence: Dysmorphic face and frontal bossing (caption); 'dysmorphic facial features and frontal bossing were observed, as shown in Figure 1'

panels.rationale: Clinical photograph of an infant's face showing frontal bossing and dysmorphic features in a case report of red cell pyruvate kinase deficiency, matching the vocabulary finding frontonasal hyperplasia; eyes are redacted with a black bar.
panels.attribution_text: Hinge et al. Red Cell Pyruvate Kinase Deficiency With Hypertriglyceridemia: A Case Report.. Cureus 2024. doi:10.7759/cureus.65839. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
in_text_mentions: was born by normal vaginal delivery. After 12 hours of life, the baby developed severe respiratory distress and indirect hyperbilirubinemia. Respiratory support was provided, and an exchange transfusion was performed for neonatal hyperbilirubinemia, followed by two days of phototherapy. The child has a history of two hospitalizations for low hemoglobin, during which packed red blood cell transfusions were administered. On head-to-toe examination, the child exhibited severe pallor and mild icterus. Additionally, dysmorphic facial features and frontal bossing were observed, as shown in Figure 1.
